response.text:
Short answer: no — the sender does not see anything different if you archive vs delete their message. Those actions only affect your copy of the mail, not what the sender sees or is told.

What happens to the message (general / Gmail-focused):

- Archive
  - Removes the message from your Inbox view (it removes the Inbox label).
  - Keeps the message in your account (it appears in "All Mail" and under any other labels it has).
  - The message is still searchable and can be moved back to the Inbox by adding the Inbox label or replying.
  - New replies to that thread will normally return it to your Inbox because they are new incoming messages.

- Delete (Trash)
  - Moves the message to your Trash/Bin.
  - In Gmail, items in Trash are permanently deleted after about 30 days (or sooner if you empty Trash).
  - While in Trash the message is not kept in All Mail and is slated for permanent removal; you can typically recover it from Trash until it’s deleted permanently.
  - Emptying Trash or permanent deletion removes the message from your account so it is no longer accessible.

Other notes:
- Neither action notifies the sender or changes their copy — it only changes how you store/view the message.
- Different mail systems/providers use slightly different names/locations for “archive” (e.g., a server “Archive” folder) and retention policies, but the same basic idea applies: archive = remove from inbox but keep; delete = mark for removal.
